doc.title: Chico Freeman interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2001

title: Playing in Elvin Jones's band
summary: He talks about the thrill of the Coltrane-lineage band, working with McCoy Tyner today, and Elvin as a sweet man with intense concentration.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: What was it like playing with Elvin Jones?

Great. I mean John Coltrane was one of my biggest influences, and to be able to have worked with everyone that was in that great band. And I did, everyone except for Jimmy Garrison, because he had passed on before I got there. But I’m working with McCoy Tyner today. I mean in fact I have a tour with him this summer, a summer tour. And I’m scheduled to go to Las Vegas with him next month. And I’ve gone to Japan with him and I’ve recorded with him. So I still work with McCoy on and off. And Elvin Jones, I was some years with him. Working with Elvin was great. I mean to have that power, that drummer that propelled Coltrane, and to understand what that meant. Not just to hear it but to feel it and be a part of it was for me a very great thing.
Those of us who don’t know him, when you watch him, you get the impression that this could be a mean person.
Oh he’s the sweetest guy you ever want to meet.
Isn’t that interesting. Because I think it’s something about — in fact I just saw a photo today of him, and he was playing, and he’s got this look on his face, you know, like wow.
I guess so. But I’m glad to hear that he’s a nice person.
No, he’s a nice guy. Working with him was an education, it was a pleasure, it was a dream come true. It was a lot of things for me. It was one of the best times with my musical life.
